description: Controlled vocabulary for the regulation requirement matrix. Every enumerated value used by a requirement record resolves to a canonical concept here.
design_note: Regime terms are NOT merged into canonical ones. `personal_information` (CCPA),
but legally distinct scopes, and collapsing them would silently assert an
equivalence no source states. Instead each regime term keeps its own identity and
declares the canonical concept it maps to, so a query can ask either
'what does CCPA call this' or 'show me every regime's equivalent' without the data
`maps_to` therefore means 'is this regime's expression of', not 'is identical to'.
Where a regime term is genuinely narrower or broader than the canonical concept,

topics.description: Canonical subject of a requirement. Replaces the free-text topic field, which had grown 45 values containing synonym clusters (international_transfer/international_transfers, children/minors/children_and_adolescents, notice/privacy_notice/privacy_policy/transparency, and others) that made topic-based lookup unreliable.

legal_bases.description: Grounds on which processing may lawfully occur. Regimes differ on which exist at all: CCPA has no general lawful-basis regime, and DPDP frames its non-consent grounds as 'legitimate uses' rather than as bases equivalent to GDPR Article 6.

legitimate_use.label: Legitimate use (DPDP)
legitimate_use.note: DPDP-specific. Deliberately not merged with legitimate_interests: the Act does not adopt the GDPR balancing test and the categories are enumerated rather than open-ended.

state_specific_consent.label: State-specific consent requirement
state_specific_consent.note: Placeholder used by the generic US state model, resolved per state.

state_specific_exception.label: State-specific exception
state_specific_exception.note: Placeholder used by the generic US state model, resolved per state.

data_categories.description: Categories of data a requirement applies to. Regime terms are preserved and mapped, never merged - see design_note.

digital_personal_data.note: DPDP covers personal data in digital form, and non-digital data subsequently digitised. Non-digital-only processing is outside its scope, so this is narrower than the canonical concept.

sensitive_personal_information.note: CPRA's SPI list is not the same set as GDPR Article 9, and the CPRA right is to limit use rather than a prohibition with conditions. Treating the two as interchangeable would be wrong.

adolescent_personal_data.note: LGPD addresses children and adolescents as distinct groups; this term is the adolescent half and does not carry the child-specific conditions.

location_data.note: Article 9 location data is defined as location data other than traffic data, and is governed by its own conditions. Added during the Phase 6C ePrivacy conversion because Article 9 had no term; it is deliberately not merged with traffic_data, which Article 6 governs differently.

covered_actors.description: The role a requirement binds. Preserved per regime because the roles are not interchangeable: a CCPA service provider is not a GDPR processor, and DPDP has no controller/processor split of the GDPR kind.

service_operator.label: Operator of the service or network

intermediary.label: Consent intermediary
intermediary.note: DPDP-specific role with no equivalent in the other Tier 1 regimes.

requirement_types.description: What kind of obligation the record expresses. Populated during normalisation because the schema declared the field but nothing set it, leaving the engine unable to distinguish a hard obligation from a scope statement.

values.scope: States when the regime applies at all. Not itself an obligation.
values.obligation: Something the covered actor must do.
values.prohibition: Something the covered actor must not do.
values.right: An entitlement of the individual that the actor must honour.
values.definition: Defines a term or category used by other requirements.

authority_levels.description: How directly the requirement is stated by the cited source. Lets the engine separate what a statute says from what an interpretation adds, which the methodology requires be kept distinct.

values.delegated: Stated in rules, regulations or delegated instruments.
values.regulator_guidance: Stated in official regulator guidance rather than binding text.
values.derived: Not stated verbatim; assembled from the cited provisions during research. Must be reviewed before being relied upon.

regions.description: ISO-style region identifiers used by applicability. Kept coarse deliberately: the matrix records where a regime asserts application, not a resolved geolocation policy.
